title: Unbounce dropped '70% lower cost-per-lead' and replaced it with 'Launch faster. Convert more.'
body: The 2019 headline **"Convert More Leads and Sales From Your Ad Spend"** and a section promising **"Lower Cost-Per-Lead By Over 70%"** targeted buyers already running paid campaigns and focused on ROI numbers. The current **"Launch faster. Convert more."** is shorter and drops the ad-spend context entirely. This likely broadens the audience beyond PPC marketers to anyone who needs landing pages built quickly.

title: Unbounce removed 'SEE HOW UNBOUNCE CAN HELP ME' and added 'Start building for free' as the primary hero CTA
body: The old CTAs — **"SEE HOW UNBOUNCE CAN HELP ME"**, **"SHOW ME HOW"**, **"PREVIEW THE LANDING PAGE BUILDER"** — all pushed visitors toward exploration before committing. The new primary CTA **"Start building for free"** skips the discovery step and asks for sign-up immediately. The shift suggests Unbounce may now rely on the product itself to convert, rather than an explanation layer in between.

title: Unbounce added 'Let AI and ML do the heavy lifting' as a section heading — a phrase absent across all pre-2024 snapshots
body: Ten new H2s were added across the period, but **"Let AI and ML do the heavy lifting"** and **"Everything you need to A/B test in one place"** represent the clearest content-architecture signal. Earlier headings like **"Mobile-responsive landing page, popup, and sticky bar templates"** described features. The newer headings describe outcomes and automation, suggesting the team now prioritises buyers who want results managed for them, not a toolset to operate manually.

title: Unbounce's page title shift from 'Landing Page Software' to 'CRO platform' spans seven years — that is a category claim, not an update
body: In 2019 the page title read **"Landing Page Builder & Conversion Platform for Marketers | Landing Page Software"**. By Jun 2026 it reads **"The Best Landing Page Builder and CRO platform | Unbounce"**. Dropping 'Software' and leading with 'Best' while adding 'CRO platform' indicates a deliberate move to compete on a broader category label. Taken alongside the headline and H2 changes, the full arc points to repositioning away from a single-tool identity toward a conversion-suite claim.
